riskDescription.context: Support has been extended at no additional cost until September 2026 without formal contractual clarity, and the original SOW and subsequent CR lacked defined end dates, scope boundaries, and commercials. EMS shows Overall RAG Red (Commercial), Cost Red, and Scope Red.
riskDescription.condition: Continued delivery effort without a signed CR or new SOW structure may result in revenue leakage and unrecoverable costs beyond the current extension period.
riskDescription.consequence: Margin erosion could accelerate, and the business may be unable to invoice for work performed, impacting project profitability and client commercial relationship.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Establish formal SOW and CR approval process with defined scope boundaries and commercial terms before extending any support activities.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: Upon failure to secure signed CR by November 30, escalate to portfolio leadership and halt extended support to prevent further revenue leakage.
risks.reasoning: Carried forward and re-rated from open EMS risks R831, R832, R833 (all Identified, Major, Very Likely, High) and corroborated by ALT Watchlist entry noting lack of formal SOW/CR and commercial clarity. Project end date: 2026-12-31.

riskDescription.context: Scope and delivery expectations are evolving without a formally approved SOW or CR, and the Red Hat–IBM organizational transition began on 1 October 2026 with IT and Security operations merging. EMS Scope RAG is Red.
riskDescription.condition: Undefined scope boundaries and evolving feature expectations may lead to uncontrolled scope expansion and misaligned delivery commitments.
riskDescription.consequence: Delivery predictability could deteriorate, client satisfaction may decline, and the project may fail to meet business outcomes within the available timeline and budget.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Implement formal scope change evaluation procedure requiring documented customer approval and impact assessment before accepting any new feature requests.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: Should scope creep exceed 15 percent of baseline, rebaseline impacted delivery plan with customer and escalate to senior leadership within 72 hours.
risks.reasoning: Carried forward from open EMS risks R831, R832, R833 and supported by ALT Watchlist noting challenges in clarity of scope and feature implementation. Red Hat–IBM merger adds governance complexity. Project end date: 2026-12-31.

riskDescription.context: The project relies on IBM for product fixes and feature delivery for the IBM Verify platform, and the Red Hat–IBM organizational transition introduced limited stakeholder availability for key decisions. ALT notes feature gaps and dependency-related delays.
riskDescription.condition: Unresolved IBM Verify product limitations or delayed fixes may block critical integration and feature delivery activities.
riskDescription.consequence: Delivery timelines could slip further, and business benefits realization may be postponed, weakening client trust and project viability.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Establish escalation process with IBM for critical product fixes, including defined SLAs and weekly status reviews to prevent delivery timeline slippage.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: Once IBM fix delay exceeds two weeks, activate workaround solution or alternative integration path and escalate to project board immediately.
risks.reasoning: Carried forward from open EMS risks R831, R832, R833 noting reliance on IBM for product fixes, and corroborated by ALT Watchlist describing Verify feature gaps and dependency delays. Project end date: 2026-12-31.

riskDescription.context: The Red Hat–IBM organizational transition began on 1 October 2026, and EMS risks note limited stakeholder availability for key decisions and uncertainty around project continuity and future funding. EMS Timeline RAG is Red.
riskDescription.condition: Governance gaps and unclear decision authority during the merger transition may delay approvals, scope alignment, and commercial negotiations.
riskDescription.consequence: Project momentum could stall, and the team may operate without clear direction, increasing the risk of misaligned deliverables and cost overruns.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Define clear decision authority hierarchy and establish backup decision-makers with documented delegation authority to prevent approval delays during organizational transition.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: When primary stakeholder is unavailable for more than five business days, activate backup approval pathway and escalate to IBM leadership immediately.
risks.reasoning: Carried forward from open EMS risks R831, R832, R833 noting limited stakeholder availability and organizational transition. ALT confirms Red Hat IT and Security merging with IBM starting 1 October 2026. Project end date: 2026-12-31.

riskDescription.context: The Producer Portal application is fully deployed to Production and technically ready. Premera planned to send registration emails to 2,500+ producers on 22 October using a big-bang rollout approach, with end-to-end registration completed for 11 users. ALT notes status awaited.
riskDescription.condition: If a critical issue is encountered during the mass producer onboarding, the rollout may need to be rolled back and remediated, delaying production adoption.
riskDescription.consequence: Client confidence in the platform could decline, production stabilization may be delayed, and the business case for the implementation may be questioned.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Conduct phased producer onboarding with pilot group of 100 users before full rollout to validate platform stability and identify critical issues early.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: Upon detection of critical production issue affecting more than 10 percent of users, activate rollback procedure and notify customer leadership immediately.
risks.reasoning: Explicitly noted as a risk in ALT Watchlist entry for Producer Portal. Big-bang rollout with limited prior user validation (11 users) increases exposure. Single-source indication from ALT. Project end date: 2026-12-31.

riskDescription.context: EMS observation OBS006481 notes that the customer has provided continuation approval for an additional three months, and three additional applications have been identified for onboarding. The project received a 3-month extension and will continue with the same team strength.
riskDescription.condition: If the scope expands to include the three new applications without corresponding capacity augmentation, the existing team may become overextended and unable to deliver quality outcomes.
riskDescription.consequence: Sprint velocity could decline, defect rates may rise, and delivery commitments for both existing and new applications may be missed.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Conduct capacity analysis for three new applications and secure resource augmentation approval before accepting additional onboarding scope into active sprints.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: Should sprint velocity drop below 80 percent baseline, prioritize critical-path work and communicate scope deferral to customer within three business days.
risks.reasoning: Derived from EMS observation OBS006481 (Open, aging 29 days) and ALT noting three additional applications identified for onboarding. No capacity increase planned per ALT. Project end date: 2026-12-31.

riskDescription.context: EMS observation OBS006482 (Open, aging 29 days) calls for finalizing the CR strategy and documenting the commercial approach, continuing direct engagement with customer leadership to establish clarity on onboarding plans, and continuing weekly status reporting. No target closure date is set.
riskDescription.condition: If customer leadership engagement and CR strategy finalization remain delayed or incomplete, alignment on scope, commercials, and onboarding plans may not be achieved before the current extension period ends.
riskDescription.consequence: The project may enter another undocumented extension period, further eroding margin and increasing the risk of unilateral client termination or scope reduction.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Schedule weekly executive touchpoints with customer leadership to finalize CR strategy and document onboarding roadmap before current extension period ends.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: If CR approval is not secured by December 15, prepare transition plan and communicate potential resource redeployment to portfolio leadership immediately.
risks.reasoning: Derived from open EMS observation OBS006482 (aging 29 days, no target closure date) and supported by ALT noting ongoing discussions around CR and new SOW structure with no ETA. Project end date: 2026-12-31.

riskDescription.context: The project implements IGA/IAM using IBM Verify on AWS under a Hybrid execution model. ALT notes that Verify implementation encountered feature gaps and dependency-related delays, and the platform is in the Integration stage.
riskDescription.condition: Unresolved feature gaps in IBM Verify may require workarounds or custom development, increasing technical debt and integration complexity.
riskDescription.consequence: Long-term platform maintainability and scalability could be compromised, and future enhancements may require disproportionate effort and cost.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Document all IBM Verify feature gaps and workarounds in technical debt register with monthly review to prioritize remediation activities.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: Should technical debt exceed 20 percent of sprint capacity, defer non-critical enhancements and communicate impact to customer stakeholders immediately.
risks.reasoning: Derived from ALT Watchlist noting IBM Verify feature gaps and dependency delays, and EMS noting the project is in Integration stage with Architecture - Integration as primary technology. Single-source indication from ALT. Project end date: 2026-12-31.
